A0233.title: Swarm Coordination Fault Tolerance & Byzantine Defense
keywords: swarm coordination fault tolerance & byzantine defense
A0233.definition: Swarm communication redundancy, byzantine fault-tolerant consensus, member-behavior anomaly detection and isolation, and swarm-level e-stop and degraded operation to prevent individual hijacked or faulty members from causing whole-swarm loss-of-control.
A0233.description:
Swarm coordination fault tolerance & byzantine defense builds four layers against the risk of individual hijacked swarm members becoming byzantine nodes, communication disruption, or algorithm defects triggering cascading loss-of-control. First, communication redundancy — multi-path communication among swarm members, so single-link disruption does not fail consensus. Second, byzantine fault-tolerant consensus (e.g., PBFT, HoneyBadger) reaches correct consensus even when some members send false information. Third, member-behavior anomaly detection identifies and isolates members deviating from swarm protocol (e.g., sending anomalous commands, trajectory deviation). Fourth, swarm-level e-stop and degraded operation — when swarm loss-of-control is detected, all members e-stop or degrade to a safe mode.

This measure is the core defense after KARGU-2 autonomous weapons and warehouse AMR swarms lose control; it works with A0232 (robot safety stop E-stop & functional-safety design) and A0108 (IoT network isolation and access control).
A0233.limitation: Byzantine fault tolerance adds communication and compute overhead; large-scale swarm consensus has high latency, hard to meet real-time control; anomaly-detection false positives can wrongly isolate normal members; swarm-level e-stop may be abused by attackers for denial of service; defense fails when members exceed the fault-tolerance threshold.
